raw_response: {"sentences":[{"text":"Leaving the Museum of Natural History behind, make your way toward the Beacon Theatre, about a sixteen-minute walk.","source_id":"GLUE_NAV","source_type":"glue","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Step inside and one critic swore it was like walking into an Arab sheik's tent, while a reporter called the whole place \"a true bit of Bagdad on Broadway.\"","source_id":"8b4e30b8-f346-4aaf-be42-bb18d5d265ec","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"That fever dream was deliberate — Ahlschlager built the Beacon as a miniature of his earlier Roxy Theatre in Midtown, and where the Roxy leaned Moorish and Renaissance, here he blended Renaissance, Ancient Roman, Ancient Greek, and Rococo into one room.","source_id":"8b4e30b8-f346-4aaf-be42-bb18d5d265ec","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Look toward the stage.","source_id":"a729320d-0845-42b3-8a62-23fbe4183146","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Doric columns hold up the proscenium arch, and flanking it stand two bronze women thirty feet tall — Greek goddesses that Women's Wear Daily dubbed \"heroic-size bronzes of Amazons with spear and shield.\"","source_id":"a729320d-0845-42b3-8a62-23fbe4183146","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Overhead, the ceiling is painted red, gold, green, and blue and shaped to hang like the draped roof of a tent.","source_id":"a729320d-0845-42b3-8a62-23fbe4183146","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"East of the vestibule, a circular rotunda carries the Rococo idea even further, its ceiling rising as high as the auditorium itself, packed with rosette and coffer moldings and a huge chandelier hanging at its center.","source_id":"6f33fd2c-c88f-4923-9b14-3d2f4e2ee19c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Above the doorways there's a landscape mural by Valdemar Kjoldgaard, hidden for years under wallpaper until the 2008 renovation stripped it away and brought the painting back.","source_id":"6f33fd2c-c88f-4923-9b14-3d2f4e2ee19c","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Down in the orchestra pit sits the theater's original Wurlitzer organ, built in 1928, with four manuals and nineteen ranks.","source_id":"6848de81-b503-4b32-b891-9438a4d52846","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"It's one of only three Manhattan theaters that still keep their original organ, alongside Radio City Music Hall and the United Palace.","source_id":"6848de81-b503-4b32-b891-9438a4d52846","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The Beacon nearly lost it — by the early 1960s the organ had been abandoned, and it survived only because ripping it out cost more than the operators wanted to spend, before a 1967 restoration put it back in service until it was sealed in 2009.","source_id":"6848de81-b503-4b32-b891-9438a4d52846","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"Since 2007, more than two thousand performers have been talked into signing their names on the walls of one elevator here — Jerry Seinfeld, Bono, Amy Poehler and Tina Fey, Trevor Noah, Ben Schwartz, Eddie Vedder.","source_id":"17a53de8-c889-4229-a65f-e9ac9fbeda33","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"But the act that truly made this room its home was the Allman Brothers Band, the most frequent performer the Beacon ever had.","source_id":"6efdfd88-6a9d-4d58-8a81-f829ac9c6275","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"They first played here in 1989, came back in 1992 and 1994, and then turned up almost every year, so reliably that a 2002 New York Times piece called their shows \"as sure a sign of spring as the reappearance of robins and bellybuttons.\"","source_id":"6efdfd88-6a9d-4d58-8a81-f829ac9c6275","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"In March 2000 they recorded a live album in this house, releasing Peakin' at the Beacon that November, and in 2009 they marked their fortieth anniversary here with shows dedicated to their founder and original frontman, Duane Allman.","source_id":"6efdfd88-6a9d-4d58-8a81-f829ac9c6275","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"A Cirque du Soleil run bumped them in 2010, but they were invited back in 2011 — and on October 28, 2014, they played the final show of their career on this stage, their 238th concert at the Beacon.","source_id":"6efdfd88-6a9d-4d58-8a81-f829ac9c6275","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"None of that was guaranteed, because in February 1986, the year Andy Feltz took over as manager, the owners announced they'd gut the Beacon into a nightclub, restaurant, and discotheque.","source_id":"ee38a2f5-2375-4464-a9c4-cc0a1895a4af","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"At the time it was the only mid-sized live-concert venue in Manhattan, since Avery Fisher Hall and Carnegie Hall, the other rooms its size, were mostly given over to classical music.","source_id":"ee38a2f5-2375-4464-a9c4-cc0a1895a4af","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The developer, Olivier Coquelin, and his architect Charles A. Platt, a former landmarks commissioner, said they'd picked the Beacon precisely for its landmark status, and promised to build the club as a freestanding structure inside the auditorium so they'd barely touch the protected interior.","source_id":"ee38a2f5-2375-4464-a9c4-cc0a1895a4af","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4},{"text":"The neighborhood didn't buy it — residents feared for the landmarked details, and preservationists banded together as the Committee to Save the Beacon Theatre to stop the whole thing.","source_id":"ee38a2f5-2375-4464-a9c4-cc0a1895a4af","source_type":"beat","stop_idx":4}]}
